purpose: Tune34 general compiler/runtime batch: fresh unchanged-source release A/B, separate workload-equivalence diagnostics, preserved Result53/Tune33 snapshots.

accepted_mechanisms: Guarded native float-to-int conversion and positive floor composition
Complete dynamic compact-int bitwise admission with finite result guard
Bounded mixed numeric local recurrence proofs
Exact numeric-position reads from stable roots with pure keys
Zeroed small runtime container construction through the existing precise size-class bump allocator
Recycled swept bump slots with stable precise ownership and consistent requested-byte accounting
Sweep dead headers before live-only data compaction; retain DFS tracing and abandon failed mark growth before weak processing
Shared inlined small-slot construction for generic and known-class allocator entries without a delegating call
remaining_proposals: General array-content finite ranges and power-of-two remainder masking
Cheaper precise-rooted scalar snapshot storage for recursive plain parameters
implementation_scope.conditional_character_append: No new ASCII allocation mechanism is justified: chr already returns shared immutable ASCII storage.

metadata.purpose: Tune34 unchanged-source Lambda qualification, with the shared 15-frame Navier migration already in the control inputs.

method_notes: Release private binaries, serialized alternating pairs under caffeinate; zero retry acceptance.

Eight untyped/typed pilots and selected controls use21pairs; all142Lambda rows have a3pair output/performance screen. Screened slowdowns have separate21pair followups. Mixed-sample aggregates are descriptive.
All71LambdaJS rows use the MIR backend:67short rows have at least3pairs, and four registered600second JQ rows have a1pair census. The latter cannot establish confidence or exclude a small regression.
Node is used for workload-content diagnostics only. Cross-language canonical timers retain the documented setup, validation, representation and semantic differences.

Profiling/compile/native-code captures are separate from accepted timing samples. Counts cover instrumented MIR helper/boxed-entry and copy paths throughout the process, including setup. They are not an exhaustive C++ call graph or CPU percentages.

Compiler phase totals cover parse/AST/analysis and the MIR pass pipeline, including finalize/link/native publication. MIR Direct charges that pass manager under transpile; the standalone mir_gen column is zero here and does not isolate native generation. Process wall samples include the combined cold startup/generation/execution cost.

comparison_matrix.name: crypto_sha1
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: 25 hashes of the same expected digest; dynamic complete bitwise and numeric-read admission retains sized/poison/error fallbacks. Recursive boxed boundaries may remain.

comparison_matrix.name: navier_stokes
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: Both current ports time 15 frames and check77. Lambda times allocation/checksum too; JS setup is before the timer. Solver fusion/content versus reference swaps remain different. Historical one-frame JS results are not used.

comparison_matrix.name: splay
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: Canonical Lambda includes setup, 50x80 modifications and node-count validation; canonical JS times modifications after setup. Matched-seed/payload diagnostics are separate. Rejected decoder is absent from final candidate.

comparison_matrix.name: brainfuck
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: 10000 Hello World interpretations with 30000-cell tape. Lambda int payloads nominally initialize 2.4 GB versus JS Uint8Array 0.3 GB. This is a source/layout byte calculation, not a sampled CPU share. Dispatch and string/native arithmetic differences remain.

comparison_matrix.name: json_gen
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: 10 x 1000 objects with seed42. Lambda floor and JS trunc differ in 750 objects; only the explicitly floor-aligned diagnostic establishes full cross-language content equality.

comparison_matrix.name: levenshtein
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: Four distances 3,3,500,2. Canonical Lambda prints inside its timer; JS prints afterwards. Separate diagnostics place output after all timers. Row snapshots and complete min tuples are optimized.

comparison_matrix.name: puzzle
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: 724 solutions on n=10. Plain-parameter recursive snapshots remain observable (S9.1.2); JS shares arrays and undoes mutations. No copy removal is claimed.

comparison_matrix.name: fft
comparison_matrix.comparison_limits: Canonical arrays have4096 floats, allzero; the plain Lambda parameter does not publish a transform. Separate returned nonzero diagnostics prove the kernel and snapshot contract. Generic mixed-domain updates can remain.
